title: Grateful Dead Live at Carousel Ballroom on 1968-03-29
lineage: AUD > ?? > CDR > EAC (secure) > Cool Edit (minor fixes) > CD Wave (retracking) > mkwACT > SHN (seekable)

ai_review.summary: A superb audience recording that captures the fire of New Potato Caboose, Morning Dew and The Other One suite with surprisingly clear sound for 1968.
ai_review.review: The March‑29‑68 Carousel tape is widely praised as the best audience capture of that year – crisp enough to rival many early soundboards – and it delivers a high‑energy set highlighted by an epic New Potato Caboose and a soaring Morning Dew.  While a few reviewers note a low‑mix bass, truncated Lovelight and a brief Born Cross‑Eyed fragment, the overall performance is regarded as a classic snapshot of the Dead’s early psychedelic peak.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers give 4–5 stars and emphasize both excellent sound quality and standout performances; only a few note minor flaws, leading to a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Exceptionally clear for an audience tape – surprisingly low noise and good instrument separation. Minor issues: Phil’s bass slightly recessed, Lovelight starts mid‑song, Born Cross‑Eyed only a fragment, some echo on the first set.

poor_songs: Cryptical > The Other One (low energy per one reviewer)
show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is solid but noted as incomplete; the second set builds momentum with New Potato and The Other One, delivering a high‑octane climax despite a brief loss of momentum after the Quick/Dead tour.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar is described as howling, sustained and at its best on New Potato; tone praised throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass sometimes low in the mix but also highlighted for deep, resonant sound and strong playing during New Potato.
